definitions.gloss: taking up a new post, assuming a new assignment
definitions.explanation: Going to a new location to begin work at an assigned position, typically involving relocation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{来月|らいげつ}→来月：00744_raigetsu⟧⟦{大阪|おおさか}→大阪：09779_oosaka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{赴任|ふにん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I'm taking up a new post in Osaka next month.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}{赴任|ふにん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{決|き}まった→決まる：01233_kimaru⟧。
examples.english: My overseas assignment has been decided.

examples.japanese: {単身|たんしん}{赴任|ふにん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{離|はな}れて→離れる：02397_hanareru⟧⟦{暮|く}らす→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧ことになった。
examples.english: Due to an unaccompanied transfer, I ended up living apart from my family.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ verb: {赴任|ふにん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to take up a new post). Implies relocation — simply starting a new job at the same location would not be {赴任|ふにん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {赴任|ふにん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to take up a new post
- {海外|かいがい}{赴任|ふにん}: overseas assignment
- {単身|たんしん}{赴任|ふにん}: unaccompanied transfer (going alone without family)
- {赴任先|ふにんさき}: assignment location, new post
- {赴任|ふにん}{手当|てあて}: relocation allowance

CULTURAL NOTE:
{単身|たんしん}{赴任|ふにん} (living apart from family due to a work transfer) is a common phenomenon in Japanese corporate life, where employees may be transferred to distant offices. The family often stays behind due to children's schooling or housing.
